answer: At most 5 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a lotus tag. The trellis cap is checked at intake and kernel reveals the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a swarm in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, because each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 15 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
